tested_scope: Exactly one deterministic self-local continuation of c29. Provider state is held fixed at logical operation O5/payload D5, current identity I7, exact mapping I7->K5@g8 and terminal provider proof P_I7_g8. Repository claim authority alone advances through current fence F9, stale replay F8, and reacquisition as F10. The fixture tests whether an otherwise valid provider proof or prior finalization record may authorize effects across repository claim-fence generations. No concrete provider, public source, O/downstream/other-worker state, shared ledger, scheduler state, hosted compute, richer-mode arbitration, finite quota, or second semantic leaf is tested.

premises: Repository claim fences are monotonically ordered ownership epochs; only the exact current fence may authorize a new finalization transition.
Provider mapping and terminal proof remain byte-for-byte unchanged across F9 -> stale F8 replay -> F10 reacquisition.
A finalization record is eligible only when operation, payload, identity, mapping generation, provider proof identity, effect digest and repository fence all match the current finalization tuple.
Historical provider evidence may remain immutable provenance, but it cannot by itself confer current repository ownership authority.
fixture.candidate_action: Under F9, R9 may authorize finalization if every tuple field matches. Replaying F8 is rejected immediately because F8 is not current even though P_I7_g8 remains valid provider evidence. After reacquisition as F10, R9 is historical-only because its fence field is F9; P_I7_g8 alone cannot carry F9 authorization into F10. Any F10 authorization requires a new fence-bound admission/finalization record R10 that names F10 and the exact same provider proof/mapping/effect tuple. This does not require rerunning the provider merely because the fence changed; it requires re-binding authorization to the current claim epoch before any effect transition is accepted.

weak_rule_falsified.rule: If provider identity, mapping generation and terminal proof are unchanged, a finalization accepted under one repository fence may be reused after a stale-fence replay or later claim reacquisition.
weak_rule_falsified.falsification: That rule collapses repository ownership epochs. R9 would remain authorizing after F10 reacquisition, allowing a stale claimant's finalization authority to survive an ABA change in claim ownership. Binding the finalization record to the exact current fence makes F8 and R9 fail under F10 while retaining P_I7_g8 only as provider evidence.

fixture.minimum_safe_rule: Separate provider evidence validity from repository authorization validity. A provider terminal proof may remain reusable evidence when its own operation/payload/identity/domain/mapping-generation scope is unchanged, but it never transports claim authority across repository-fence generations. Every accepted effect/finalization transition must carry a current-fence-bound record over {operation,payload,idempotency identity,provider mapping generation,provider proof identity,effect digest,current repository fence}. Any prior-fence record becomes historical-only immediately when the fence advances.

observations: Stale fence F8 is rejected even though provider proof P_I7_g8 remains unchanged and otherwise valid.
After F10 reacquisition, prior finalization record R9 is historical-only because its repository-fence field no longer matches current authority.
The minimum safe construction need not force a duplicate provider execution; it must force a fresh current-fence authorization binding before an effect transition can be accepted.
inference: Within this deterministic fixture, recurring-Chat coordination can defend against repository-fence ABA without hosted coordination by treating provider proof and repository authorization as independent monotonic predicates. Lightweight repository state can retain immutable provider evidence while requiring a current-fence-bound finalization record for each ownership epoch. This narrows the required mechanism more precisely than a rule that discards all provider evidence on every fence change.
